title: Workforce management
blurb: Forecast volume and AHT, staff to a target, and keep IEX as a different product.

lessons.title: What CXone WFM is for
lessons.summary: CXone WFM forecasts, schedules, and checks adherence. The welcome page lists the modules and a 10,000-agent scale. IEX is a different application.
objectives: Not merge IEX into CXone WFM

p: The welcome page says CXone WFM manages and forecasts agent schedules. After agents and groups are set up you forecast, edit, and generate a schedule. You can create shift bids, review time off, and check adherence.
It supports tenants up to 10,000 agents. Scheduling, Forecasting, Intraday, Real-Time Adherence, Time Off, and Reporting are certified at that scale.
If you use Workforce Management (IEX Integrated), the page says the relevant help is inside that application.
Bullseye sends IEX users to the Distribution Rules Guide and CXone WFM users to the online help.

lessons.title: Forecast volume and AHT
lessons.summary: History becomes a volume and AHT forecast. You need at least three months, and the page also recommends at least 13 weeks. Then you generate staffing.
objectives: Name AHT as the page does
Know data can change after staffing

p: Accurate results need at least three months of historical data. When you define the period, the page recommends at least 13 weeks. You choose how many months and an end date. The start date is set for you.
Received values come from historical ACD reports. Forecast data can change after you generate the staffing plan.
The page says WFM runs time-series models and checks them against history. It names ideas such as day-of-week splits, a whole time series, ARIMA, exponential smoothing, and curve fitting.
If recent Fridays are unusually low, ARIMA may predict extreme drops. The page suggests comparing exponential smoothing and reviewing outliers. This lesson does not pick a model for you.

lessons.title: The service target is a staffing choice
lessons.summary: The page's example is answering in under 10 seconds instead of 30. The tighter target needs more people. Bullseye can change who those people are.
objectives: Not invent an Erlang formula as NiCE's
Tell WFM when the pool changes

p: Lowering average speed of answer needs more agents. So does raising dials. The staffing plan is the last step of that story.
This lab does not claim NiCE uses a particular published Erlang formula. The product describes its own engine and models.
If bullseye changes who can answer, the plan's 'people' are a different set. Read the WFM guidance first.
What-If lets you compare alternates without pretending the history changed.

lessons.title: Schedules, bids, and time off
lessons.summary: After the forecast you edit and generate the schedule. Agents can bid on shifts. Time off is requested and reviewed. The welcome page names those jobs without this lesson inventing the screens.
objectives: Put bids and time off after the forecast
Keep intraday as the day-of module

p: The welcome page says you forecast, edit, and generate a schedule, create bids agents can bid on, review time-off requests, and check adherence.
Intraday and Real-Time Adherence are in the certified module list, so the day-of picture is a product surface, not an afterthought.
Button-level steps for bids are not copied here. Open the current WFM help for the screen you are on, and do not follow IEX clicks if you are in CXone WFM.
A schedule that ignores a bullseye change is the routing lesson's failure mode.

lessons.title: Real-time adherence
lessons.summary: RTA compares agent state to the schedule. The UCCE and Avaya connectors exist so a non-CXone ACD can feed that picture. Historical adherence is a separate pull.
objectives: Not expect RTA to fix routing

p: Real-Time Adherence is one of the modules certified at the 10,000-agent scale. It is not the forecast and not the script.
A wrong bullseye window produces long waits. RTA will show agents in a state. It will not rewrite the script.

The UCCE connector supplies real-time agent states and historical data. Historical skill data uses SQL against the Cisco database on a 15-minute interval. Historical adherence is also pulled every 15 minutes.
Avaya CMS is a different connector, also for RTA and history, using an access key.

lessons.title: IEX is not a skin on CXone WFM
lessons.summary: The welcome page sends IEX users to help inside IEX. Bullseye sends them to the Distribution Rules Guide. Do not screenshot one product to train the other.
objectives: Keep the 10,000 sentence on CXone WFM

p: Workforce Management (IEX Integrated) has its own help, inside the application. The CXone WFM welcome page says so in the first lines.
The 10,000-agent sentence is on the CXone WFM page. Do not paste it onto IEX.
CXone WFM: online help. IEX: Distribution Rules Guide. The page tells you to decide before you configure proficiency ranges.
A migration from IEX to CXone WFM is a product move, not a theme change. This lab does not invent the migration steps.

lessons.title: Hand a routing change to WFM
lessons.summary: A one-page note is enough: priorities, windows, PC at acceleration 0, and which product. What-If is optional. Silence is how the Monday schedule goes wrong.

p: Include initial priorities, the formula you used, PC acceleration 0 if outbound is blended, and the proficiency window before and after the wait.
Say whether attributes are in use. The bullseye page's example is language plus proficiency.
